evidence_quotes.their_agenda: MISSING — Nicole never asks 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' She probes logistics immediately without establishing the customer's agenda first.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer that would require two-layer follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Nicole covers property type (house), stories (two), bedrooms (three), square footage (1800), garage (two car, full), items to move (washer/dryer, two refrigerators, king and two full bedroom sets, large couch, TV stand, desk, armchair, dining table with six chairs, grill, trampoline), and destination address. She also asks about driveway parking and additional stops.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: 'For a typical 1800 square footage home we usually expect to see around eighty to 100 box system to move. Do you think you'll fall within that range?' — asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Nicole provides: 'For a typical 1800 square footage home, it usually takes around seven to nine hours to completely move locally with three movers and one truck. In your case... I will estimate your move to take around eight to nine hours with four movers and two trucks... It's good to budget around $3,564 to $3,972... actually around $3,864 to $4,272.' Personalized to the customer's two-story home, full garage, and two-truck requirement.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Nicole discloses: hourly rate ($204 per hour, then adjusted to $102 per mover), travel fees ($300 per truck), what's included (fuel, truck, taxes, insurance, pads, tools, assembly/reassembly), no hidden fees, time-based billing, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, no deposit, no cancellation fees. All disclosed before customer asks.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: MISSING — Nicole never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or any equivalent. She moves directly to the explicit ask without checking in on the price.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Nicole states: 'We have on time guarantee if we cannot make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final Al bill. And the way the clock works is the time start as soon as we get on site and open the contract you have us for as long as you need us for any move.' The discount-on-late framing is present.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Nicole states: 'We have no worries, damage coverage. We provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for any accidental damages.' She covers the $2,000 and the purpose, but does NOT explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' — customer later asks 'is there any other additional insurance that we can purchase' suggesting the no-fine-print framing was not fully clear. Missing the no-deductible/no-fine-print framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No — Nicole delivers the Two Promises but never asks 'Does that put those to rest?' or any equivalent. She does not close the loop after the Two Promises section.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Nicole asks 'Do you have any questions or anything for me?' — this is a throwaway 'any questions' phrasing, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' version.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: MISSING — Nicole never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Nicole asks: 'And would you like our help with your move?' — asked plainly, no built-in out. The customer deflects to wanting the quote in writing, but Nicole does follow up by confirming email and offering phone/call-back options to book. The ask itself is clean.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: MISSING — Nicole never mentions 'rate lock' or that the quoted price is locked in until booking.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial — Nicole confirms email (mag.Wilson 319 @gmail.com), mentions open hours (9:00 AM to 5:30 PM), and tells the customer to reply to the email or call to book. However, she does NOT confirm date (October 29th was discussed but not re-confirmed as booked), phone number (customer said it was the current number but Nicole did not explicitly read it back or confirm), arrival window, crew size (four movers and two trucks were discussed but not confirmed as part of the booking), or notes about the customer's concerns (trampoline disassembly limitation, garage full of items) left for the crew. Major gaps.

top_strength: Nicole gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, stories, bedrooms, square footage, garage type and fullness, all furniture and appliances, special items like the trampoline), probed thoughtfully, and delivered a well-anchored, personalized estimate with full pricing transparency upfront.
coaching_note: Section 1 must open with the quid pro quo framing and wait for a yes before probing logistics; Section 2 must ask for the customer's agenda and concerns before diving into property details; and Section 7 must confirm all booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, crew notes) before the call ends — currently none of that was confirmed.
